FaqSection.title: Trading rules, explained clearly
FaqSection.description: Key answers from the official rules page covering challenge types, drawdown, conduct, payouts, and account policies.
FaqSection.noResults: No matching rule questions found. Try a different search term or category.

q1.question: What trading programs are offered?
q1.answer: Range4ex offers exactly three account types: Two Step, One Step, and Instant. Evaluation paths use defined targets, while Instant begins in the performance stage under tighter risk rules.

q2.question: What profit targets apply to each plan?
q2.answer: Two Step uses an 8% Phase 1 target and 5% Phase 2 target. One Step uses a single 10% target. Instant has no evaluation target.

q3.question: How is Daily Drawdown calculated?
q3.answer: Daily Drawdown is equity-based. The permitted daily loss is a fixed percentage of the initial account size, resets at 00:00 server time, and does not move upward with profits.

q4.question: What are the overall drawdown limits?
q4.answer: All overall drawdown is static and equity-based: Two Step is 10%, One Step is 6%, and Instant is 5%. Each breach floor is fixed from the initial account size and never trails profits.

q5.question: Is news trading allowed?
q5.answer: Opening or closing a position on an affected instrument is not allowed within 2 minutes before or after a high-impact news release. Profit generated during that restricted window is removed as a soft breach if no drawdown breach also occurred.

q6.question: Are Expert Advisors and automation allowed?
q6.answer: Personally coded automation is allowed only when it represents the trader own strategy and does not exploit latency, tick scalping, or unrealistic execution. Commercial or shared EAs sold to multiple traders are prohibited.

q7.question: What is the funded-stage profit split?
q7.answer: The standard Performance Fee split is 80% to the trader and 20% to the firm. Once an account reaches the Funded Stage, drawdown, leverage, and conduct rules continue, but no further profit target applies.

q8.question: When can a funded trader request a payout?
q8.answer: Approved payouts are processed within 2 to 5 business days. The first funded payout requires at least 5 trading days and a minimum profit. Open positions must be closed before submitting a payout request.

q9.question: When is KYC required?
q9.answer: Identity verification is required before the first payout is released on any account. The person who completes KYC must be the person placing trades on the account.

q10.question: Are evaluation fees refundable?
q10.answer: Evaluation fees for Two Step and One Step accounts may be refunded with the first successful payout, depending on the firm commercial model. Instant fees are non-refundable because there is no evaluation gate.
